title: Healey and Minogue Clash Over Affordability and Energy Policy in Final Debate
text:
Democratic incumbent Gov. Maura Healey and Republican challenger Mike Minogue debated key issues including the high cost of living, housing, and natural gas pipeline policies in their final encounter before Election Day.
Democratic incumbent Gov. Maura Healey and Republican Mike Minogue debate Oct. 15, 2026, at WCVB-TV's studio in Needham, Mass. In the final governor’s debate before Election Day, Republican businessman Mike Minogue and Democratic incumbent Gov.
Maura Healey argued over whether Massachusetts needs new leadership to improve its affordability challenges or if the state is already on the right path. , Minogue, a former CEO of a medical device company, attacked Healey over the high cost of living in Massachusetts, including electricity, while the governor defended her record on tax cuts and housing policy.
The candidates argued over Healey’s actions related to a former official in her administration who was fired after an arrest on cocaine trafficking and earlier this week charged with federal fraud in a food benefits program. Healey said during the debate she stopped natural gas pipelines from coming into the state when she was the state attorney general because the pipeline developer wanted “ratepayers and not the developer, not the company, to pay for it.
I stood up for ratepayers and I went to court. ”that found Massachusetts didn’t need new natural gas pipelines to maintain power grid reliability through 2030. Her office followed up in early 2016 by fighting pipeline developers in court toa plan that could have required ratepayers to subsidize construction costs. A 2016 state Supreme Court ruling barred the funding mechanism, and developers shelved both multi-billion-dollar proposals.
The analysis Healey’s office released estimated the bill could save electric and gas customers $11.58 billion to $14.35 billion over 10 years. It says the projected savings would come from reducing certain energy bill charges and changing utility oversight. , a conservative advocacy group, said the estimate was inflated because it did not reflect the bill’s costs for ratepayers, including expenses associated with utility programs and grid improvements. ’s latest available data.
Massachusetts residential electricity cost 30.49 cents per kilowatt hour, exceeded only by Hawaii , California and Maine .
“Someone can get 18 pounds of cocaine delivered, and you didn’t fire them. They got arrested, then they got severance, and now they’re on SNAP benefits that you didn’t even check on. ”: “If someone is arrested, you didn’t fire them. They got arrested with 18 pounds of cocaine.
In the real world, you’re automatically fired. Then you don’t get a severance package, and then you don’t get to get SNAP benefits. ”after Healey learned he was arrested Oct. 28, 2025, for trafficking cocaine after authorities seized about 17 pounds of the drug addressed to the state office building where Cook worked.he had less than $100 in his bank account and was living in a two-person household of himself and his child.
Cook’s annual salary before he was fired was about $130,000. Authorities found he had a bank account with more than $8,800 and received thousands of dollars in additional deposits, including payments from his mother who had recently won $1 million in the lottery. Cook failed to disclose that his fiancée and her mother lived with him at his Springfield residence and his fiancée earned annual income exceeding $80,000, prosecutors said.
Minogue’s description of a “severance package” was likely in reference to a vacation payout. The U.S. Attorney’s Officethe state paid Cook $22,374.29 in net pay for accrued vacation leave following his firing. Healey’s administration later realized an error in paying Cook for accrued vacation leave time and attempted to get it back but couldn’t, prosecutors said. Healey: “We have the fourth fastest growth — economic growth, GDP — in the country right now.
”by the average of the past four quarters of annualized GDP growth, Massachusetts is tied for 17th in the nation. Minogue: “In the last debate, Gov. Healey said ‘Massachusetts is a great place to live if you can afford it. ’”, Healey was asked whether she supported a ballot measure that would encourage the construction of denser housing.
She said yes.
“We need more homes,” Healey said. “Massachusetts is a great place to live if you can afford it, and that’s why I’ve been building homes from the get go. ”In tonight’s debate, Healey accused President Donald Trump of pursuing policies including tariffs that have increased the cost of building housing. PolitiFact Chief Correspondent Louis Jacobson, Senior Correspondent Amy Sherman, Staff Writers Samantha Putterman, Loreben Tuquero and Cami Henry-Seymore and PolitiFact New York Reporter Conor Amendola contributed to this report.

He made hundreds of millions of dollars scamming people. ”President Donald Trump has deported “over 13,000 Cubans since he has been in office, his first term and his second term. ”For President Donald Trump, “there’s no financial gain like the past presidents have had.
